title: KV shard alignment: seqlen cliff scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Intermittent token corruption observed when clients push sequences near 65k tokens (rare). Behavior: model outputs start repeating a 32-token window from earlier context then jumps to a different earlier window. Looks like prefix served from wrong shard/offset.
- Triggered more frequently under attention kernel 'auto-select' when sequence-length distribution has heavy tail. Suspect shard alignment + KV index rollover interplay.

Observed when:
- Dedicated cluster n1-gpu-4; 4xA100, kernel selector picks tiled-attn v2 for typical sequences but falls back to chunked-kv path for very long sequences.
- Sessions with aggressive prefix caching (prefix_cache=true) and reuse across conversations.

Repro attempts (commands run locally against repro harness):
```
# baseline repro (single worker)
python tests/repro_seq_cliff.py --model rdm-13b-qlora --seq 66000 --seed 42 --use-prefix-cache --kernel auto-select
# run under sanitizer
PYTHONMALLOC=debug python -m pytest tests/test_kv_index.py::TestIndexRollover::test_wraparound -k long
# run with env debug flags
REDWOOD_DEBUG_KV=1 REDWOOD_KERNEL_TRACE=1 python tools/trace_session.py --session-id repro-20250921
```

Key logs (trimmed):
- from trace_session.log at 00:12:43:
  KV_INDEX: write shard=3 offset=1048575 len=4096 -> rollover-> shard=0 offset=0
  KV_LOOKUP: session=abcd prefix_hit shard=3 offset=1048447 len=2048
  ATTENTION_FETCH: kernel=chunked-kv fetch shard=0 offset=64 len=32768
  ATTENTION_MERGE: merged kv window 0x7f... != index pointer 0x7e... -> warning: kv-pointer-mismatch

- runtime stderr at crash: 
  ERROR: KVCacheReadError: fetched-offset 64 > expected-offset 1048447
  Stack: serving_runtime/kvcache/reader.py:112 -> attention/kernel_selector.py:78 -> serving_runtime/inference.py:301

Hypotheses (brainstorm):
- H1: Rollover race: write rollover increments internal epoch but reader uses stale shard mapping due to delayed metadata propagation. Long sequences hit the rollover boundary more often.
- H2: Kernel selector path split: auto-select path uses two different KV addressing schemes (absolute offset vs per-shard relative) and a conversion bug yields mixing. Happens when selector switches mid-session (short->long).
- H3: Prefix cache reuse with sharded KV: cached prefixes store (shard, relative_offset) but lookup assumes global offset; when rollover happens cached entries map to wrong shard.
- H4: Compaction/eviction race: background eviction moved older entries and reclaimed offsets that later were re-used, and reader's validation window missed the update.

What I tried to confirm each hypothesis:
- H1 tests:
  - Added verbose metadata sync logs (kvcache.metadata) to repro harness. Observed 120ms window between write-rollover and metadata refresh on worker B. Increased metadata propagation to be synchronous; repro rate dropped from 7/100 to 1/100 but didn't disappear. Suggests race contributes but not sole cause.

- H2 tests:
  - Forced kernel selection to 'chunked-kv' only and 'tiled-attn' only. Repro reproduced only with mixed-mode (start tiled then switched to chunked) runs. When pinned to a single kernel for whole session, failure rate ~0/200.
  - Code grep: attention/kernel_selector.py has two codepaths: one returns (shard_id, global_offset) the other returns (relative_offset). Found comment TODO about consistent addressing. There is a single-line conversion in kvcache/reader: if offset < SHARD_THRESHOLD: treat as relative. That heuristic fails when global offsets wrap.

- H3 tests:
  - Inspected prefix cache entries on disk: prefix-cache stores a header with 'base_shard' and 'base_epoch' but lookup reads only base_shard and recomputes offset using session.global_base which wasn't updated after rollover. Repro: manually updated prefix-cache post-rollover and lookup succeeded.

- H4 tests:
  - Dumped eviction logs: GC ran and freed offsets 0-8191 around the same time as rollover; but freed offsets are then reallocated. Readers perform an epoch check but only for full-shard resets, not per-offset reuse.

Minimal repro that toggles issue reliably (50%):
- open session with seq ~ 60k using tiled-attn
- append a random 4k chunk to push writer over shard boundary while a concurrent reader is fetching cached prefix
- kernel selector flips to chunked-kv for the new chunk

Workarounds found so far (temporary):
- Pin kernel selection to a single path per session: add session flag kernel_force=chunked|tiled. Practically reduces failures but increases latency for long sequences.
- Turn off prefix_cache for sessions expected to cross shard boundary: prefix_cache=false. This reduces throughput but avoids stale cached offsets mapping.
- Increase metadata sync frequency: set KV_METADATA_SYNC_MS=50 -> reduces but not eliminates repro.

Concrete fixes to try (ranked):
1) Unify addressing: ensure kernel selector always returns addresses in canonical global offset space. Add explicit conversion with tests. (high impact, invasive)
2) Make prefix-cache entries include epoch/version and validate on lookup; on mismatch force re-resolve. (medium impact, low risk)
3) Make rollover commit visible synchronously for any session that wrote to boundary (fast path), with background async for others. (medium impact, ops cost)
4) Harden reader: if fetched-offset vs expected-offset mismatch, fall back to re-fetch index metadata and retry N times before erroring. (low-risk patch)

Notes on tests to add:
- unit: kernel_selector returns canonical address for set of simulated inputs including wraparound cases; assert equality with direct_kv_addressing().
- integration: session replay that forces kernel flip at shard boundary and asserts no data mismatch after 1000 iterations.
- chaos: introduce artificial delay in metadata propagation and ensure read-retry recovers.

Next steps (short):
- PR to add conversion layer in kernel_selector with small unit test (I can draft): INF-3245 branch 'kernel-address-unify'.
- Add validation header to prefix-cache entries (Leena), quick patch to invalidate on mismatch.
- SRE: schedule a low-traffic deploy to test sync-on-rollover toggle.

Open questions / things to confirm:
- Does hardware memory mapping (NVMM) have a role when offsets cross GPU-local boundaries? Marcus to confirm.
- Can we accept per-session kernel pinning as config for Dedicated customers? Product question.
- Is per-offset epoch checks feasible performance-wise at our QPS? Need benchmark.

Scratch command snippets for quick local iter:
```
# force mixed kernel selector to reproduce quickly
python tests/repro_seq_cliff.py --model rdm-13b --seq 60000 --force-kernel-schedule "tiled:0-60k,chunked:60k-66k" --repeat 200
# dump prefix cache header
python tools/dump_prefix_cache.py /var/lib/redwood/prefix_cache/session-abcd | head -n 60
# quick validation retry patch (dev)
git checkout -b INF-3245/kernel-address-unify
# run integration locally with metadata slowness
REDWOOD_DEBUG_SLOW_METADATA=120 python -m pytest tests/integration/test_kernel_rollover.py::test_mixed_kernel_no_mismatch -q
```

Personal notes: keep this doc as the scratchpad; will move decisions to confluence once we pick a path. If we do small reader retry, deploy behind feature flag first.

Triage summary (for quick read):
- Failure mode: KV reads return offsets from wrong shard after rollover when kernel selection flips mid-session and prefix caching is enabled.
- Likely root: inconsistent addressing convention between kernels + stale prefix metadata.
- Immediate mitigation: kernel pinning or disable prefix_cache for heavy-tail sessions; add reader retry.
- Long-term: unify addressing and add epoch/version checks in prefix-cache.
